summary.tldr: Modernizes a standard ResNet-50 step-by-step using Vision Transformer design choices (inverted bottleneck, 7x7 depthwise conv, LayerNorm, GELU), matching Swin Transformer accuracy and scalability.
keyTakeaways: Proved pure convolutional networks can match or exceed Vision Transformers in accuracy, speed, and FLOP efficiency.
Identified critical design choices: 7x7 depthwise conv, inverted bottleneck ratio 1:4, LayerNorm instead of BatchNorm, and GELU activations.
Achieves 87.8% top-1 ImageNet accuracy with ConvNeXt-XLarge while maintaining pure CNN simplicity.

motivation.problemStatement: The rapid ascent of Vision Transformers led many researchers to assume CNNs were intrinsically limited by inductive bias and destined for obsolescence in the 2020s.
previousLimitations: Classic ResNets used outdated training recipes (SGD, basic augmentations).
ResNet bottleneck blocks placed heavy computation on 3x3 standard convolutions rather than depthwise layers.
ResNets relied on frequent BatchNorm layers, causing training-inference discrepancies.
motivation.coreInsight: By systematically applying modern Vision Transformer design principles (macro design, inverted bottlenecking, large 7x7 depthwise kernels, micro design tweaks) to a plain ResNet, a pure CNN matches or outperforms Swin Transformer across all visual tasks.
contributions: Constructed the ConvNeXt model family (Tiny, Small, Base, Large, XLarge).
Provided a transparent step-by-step modernization roadmap from ResNet-50 to ConvNeXt.
Demonstrated superior throughput, simplicity, and ease of deployment over Swin Transformer.

innovations.title: ConvNeXt Block (7x7 Depthwise Inverted Bottleneck)
innovations.summary: Combines a 7x7 depthwise convolution with an inverted bottleneck (1x1 expansion to 4x channels, GELU, 1x1 projection).
innovations.detailedDescription: Positioning the 7x7 depthwise convolution before channel expansion mimics the self-attention block placement in Transformers, reducing FLOPs while expanding the effective receptive field.

math.explanation: ConvNeXt block structure featuring 7x7 depthwise filtering followed by 1:4 channel expansion and projection.

variables.description: Layer Normalization operating on channel dimension

math.significance: Expands receptive field to 7x7 matching Transformer local window size while retaining pure CNN speed.

codeSnippet.code:
class ConvNeXtBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim):
        super().__init__()
        self.dwconv = nn.Conv2d(dim, dim, kernel_size=7, padding=3, groups=dim) # 7x7 DW Conv
        self.norm = LayerNorm(dim, eps=1e-6)
        self.pwconv1 = nn.Linear(dim, 4 * dim) # 1:4 expansion
        self.act = nn.GELU()
        self.pwconv2 = nn.Linear(4 * dim, dim) # projection
    def forward(self, x):
        shortcut = x
        x = self.dwconv(x)
        x = self.norm(x)
        x = self.pwconv1(x)
        x = self.act(x)
        x = self.pwconv2(x)
        return shortcut + x

ablationStudies.title: Kernel Size Scaling (3x3 up to 11x11)
ablationStudies.description: Evaluated impact of depthwise kernel size on model top-1 accuracy.
ablationStudies.removedComponent: 7x7 depthwise kernel (replaced with standard 3x3 depthwise kernel)
ablationStudies.performanceDelta: Increasing kernel size from 3x3 to 7x7 improved top-1 accuracy by 0.7%, while 11x11 showed no further gain.

evidence.reproducibilityNotes: Trained using AdamW with weight decay 0.05, Mixup, CutMix, RandAugment, and LayerScale initialization.

criticalNotes.title: Pure CNN Hardware Compatibility
criticalNotes.content: Contains no complex window shifting or quadratic self-attention, enabling seamless TensorRT and CoreML deployment.

criticalNotes.title: 7x7 Depthwise Kernel Memory Overhead
criticalNotes.content: 7x7 depthwise convolutions require updated cuDNN libraries to achieve maximum execution speed.

researchGaps: Can ConvNeXt principles be combined with multi-axis self-attention in hybrid architectures?

reference.originalAbstract: The 'Roaring 20s' of visual recognition began with the introduction of Vision Transformers (ViTs). In this work, we re-examine the design spaces and test the limits of what a pure ConvNet can achieve. We gradually modernize a standard ResNet toward the design of a Vision Transformer.
